items.evidence: The 'reload and verify' step (spec.ts lines 118-125 of the diff) reloads the page and checks nameInput toHaveValue(NEW_NAME) and title(NEW_NAME). If the mutation never ran, these assertions would fail.
AC1: the header title is asserted after saving (diff line 113). AC2: the name field and the title are both asserted after reload (diff lines 121-122).

No existing page object covers the product details page (e2e/pages has only addressDialog, draftOrderPage, homePage, loginPage and orderPage), and the change adds no duplicate GraphQL helper or scenario constant. It reuses PRODUCTS.hoodie.name.
No waitForTimeout, sleep or fixed-delay polling.
Imports test from ../../fixtures/test.ts, is not tagged parallel(), and does not write to the cache or the dumps.

Uses test ids and role locators. The name input is scoped to the general-settings card, and search rows are narrowed with filter({ hasText }). button-bar-confirm is used the same way existing page objects use it.
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO's existing E2E Hoodie. The only UI write is the rename under test.
No hard-coded ids: the product is reached by searching for the scenario's known name.
Uses the default admin session through the fixture, with no UI login or credentials. The ticket names no specific permission.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0. The spec is under e2e/tests/products/.
All locators and the open, rename and save actions live on ProductPage. The spec only asserts on those locators and on page URL and title.
Fields are readonly and initialised from this.page, with constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (diff lines 93, 97).
One test with three test.step stages.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e #products.
A header block comment (diff lines 80-85) explains what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first.
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO and PRODUCTS.hoodie.name. NEW_NAME is a named constant for a value no scenario defines.
No cleanup and no unique or timestamped names.
No custom timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep .ts. The page object imports expect from @playwright/test, as draftOrderPage and homePage already do. The spec takes test and expect from the fixture.
No any, no casts and no gql calls.

structured_output.summary: This is a solid submission. It adds a ProductPage page object and a single-story spec that renames E2E Hoodie from ORDERS_SCENARIO. It then proves the new name was saved by reloading and checking both the name field and the header title. It type-checks, uses the fixture and the scenario constants, and follows the locator and page-object conventions. The only finding is minor (M13): leftover generated '// spec:' and '// seed:' header comments, one of which points to a non-existent e2e/tests/seed.spec.ts.
